name: Atlassian
one_liner: Builds Jira, Confluence and Trello; interviews reward runnable, tested code in your own IDE, a code design round, and a values interview.

levels.intern: Software Engineer Intern (no P level). Summer internship for penultimate-year students; region calendars differ (US May to Sep, India May to Aug, ANZ Nov to Feb).
levels.new_grad: P30 (Levels.fyi label 'Junior Engineer'; posted as Graduate Software Engineer / SWE-1). New grads join the 12-month Grad++ program.
levels.early_career: P30 for roughly 0 to 2 yrs; P40 (Software Engineer II, Levels.fyi label 'Engineer') for roughly 2 to 5 yrs. Hiring committee sets the final level and downlevels are common.

process_new_grad.details: Apply via the Interns/Graduates filter on the careers site. Rolling review. Official recruiting windows: US and Canada Sep to Mar (grad start July), India Jul to Dec (grad start July), ANZ Feb to Jun (grad start February).

Official early careers guide: SWE candidates take an online coding test and must clear it to interview. Reported formats: HackerRank, about 90 min, 2 to 4 DSA questions (India 2026 grad drive had at least 4, incl. 'Count Bitonic Subsequences'); 2027-grad India OA (Aug 2026) asked a weighted 'make array distinct' problem. UK SWE Graduate (Sep 2026) reported psychometric assessments as round one.
About 15 min: standard eligibility checks and motivation questions, followed by 2 technical rounds (Graduate Software Engineer review, Aug 2025; location not stated in the review).

Official guide: craft interviews (technical) plus leadership and values interviews, STAR format. For SWE grads this is usually 1 to 2 coding interviews of 45 to 60 min (DSA in your own IDE, sometimes a code design problem), a values interview (45 min) and sometimes a manager/leadership interview. A P30 (SWE-1, India, Sep 2026) report shows a two-part DSA problem (longest constant-difference streak, then allow one replacement).

A hiring committee reviews all feedback independently and decides (official). Team matching follows; 2025 to 2026 reports describe P40/backend candidates waiting weeks for team match or being put on hold until headcount opened (Sep 2025 backend hire; Jan 2026 P40).

process_intern.details: Penultimate-year Bachelor's or Master's students in CS or related fields; rolling review, apply early. About 300 to 500 interns a year is a third-party figure (unverified).

HackerRank-style OA. Reports: US intern OA of 90 min with 2 or 3 questions (applied Sep 2025, SF); 2 LC mediums (US intern, interviewed Nov 2024); 3 LeetCode questions (SF intern, 2025 review); Sydney 2026 OA described as 'reasonably balanced in difficulty'; India campus OLT 2 to 3 questions around Codeforces 1600 (DP, graphs, bitmasking), with 2+ solved needed to shortlist.

Live coding with one engineer over Zoom: LeetCode easy-medium with emphasis on approach, clarity and communication (rank-teams-by-votes style hash map voting, LCA, LRU cache, intervals). NEW in 2026: several intern loops (Sydney Apr to May 2026; Guwahati and Kharagpur campus drives Aug 2026) used a 1-hour AI-assisted coding interview in a HackerRank IDE, e.g. fixing a bug in a small backend web app with an AI agent. Frontend interns build a UI component (e.g. nested bullet list).

30 to 45 min with an engineer or engineering manager, questions mapped to each Atlassian value; India campus loops call this the HR or 'LNV' round. Some loops add a recruiter call before the final round.
US intern timeline example: applied Sep 9, OA Sep 20, round 1 Oct 18, round 2 Nov 3, offer call Nov 9 (2025 cycle). Sydney candidates report 3 to 4 months end to end.

process_experienced_notes: For 1 to 3 yrs (P30/P40) the loop is staged. Screen: Karat third-party interview (60 min: about 20 min of 5 rapid-fire system design scenarios plus 2 easy-medium DSA problems), reported for P30 and P40 in 2025; an Oct 2026 candidate was told the technical screen is 20 min coding plus 15 min HLD. Stage 1: 2 coding interviews of 60 min each, Data Structures (own IDE, tests, debugger allowed) and Code Design. Official prep PDFs dated Jul and Aug 2026 say Code Design is now AI-enabled: a HackerRank IDE with AI coding assistants and an existing code repository you extend, fix or refactor, in a language you may not know. Stage 2: 60-min system design (ladder of follow-ups). Stage 3: 60-min management interview (own outcomes, expertise-driven improvements, initiative, team contribution) and 45-min values interview. Each stage is gated by recruiter feedback. Hiring committee then levels you; candidates report being downleveled P50 to P40 for skipping clarifying questions in design.
timeline: Official: interviews are scheduled in stages and the recruiter confirms progression after each; a hiring committee decides after the loop; team matching happens after the hiring committee (centralized hiring, not team-first). Reported: US intern about 2 months (Sep to Nov 2025); Sydney intern 3 to 4 months; P40 backend about 2 months from recruiter reply to HC approval, including almost a month of year-end HC wait (Jan 2026; location not stated); P50 loop Dec 6 2025 to Jan 9 2026 with HC verdict Jan 20. Recruiting seasons per region on the early careers page. CHANGE: Atlassian announced layoffs of about 10% of its workforce in March 2026 (Wikipedia); 2026 LeetCode posts describe paused team matches and a re-test via the AI-assisted round for a pre-layoff hire.

oa.platform: HackerRank (India 2026-grad internship drive screenshot); an Atlassian-branded timed IDE with sections was used for the 2027-grad OA (Aug 2026). UK graduate track started with psychometric tests (Sep 2026).
oa.format: 2 to 4 coding questions, about 90 min (US intern 2025); India campus OLT 2 to 3 questions of roughly Codeforces 1600 difficulty (DP, graphs, bitmasking, greedy, XOR). Sydney: 2 medium plus 1 easy. Data engineering intern OAs mix SQL and LeetCode.
oa.notes: OA is mandatory for early careers (official). Reported 2026 OA problems: count bitonic subsequences mod 1e9+7 (HackerRank, Q4 of 4); minimum total cost to make all array values distinct when incrementing A[i] costs C[i]. India campus shortlists are small (one 2024 campus: 15 shortlisted, 5 offers).

coding.rounds: Intern and new grad: 1 to 2 coding interviews (45 to 60 min). P30/P40 experienced loop: 2 coding interviews of 60 min (Data Structures + Code Design), after a Karat or technical screen.
coding.style: LeetCode easy to medium for interns; medium (sometimes hard, e.g. All O`one) for P40, usually wrapped in an Atlassian product story (Jira activity, Confluence audit logs, support agent ratings, voting). Code design problems are multi-part and extensible (Snake game, tennis court booking with maintenance breaks, middleware router with wildcards, rate limiter, customer/product rating system). Some loops add concurrency follow-ups (P60 customer rating code design, Feb 2026).
coding.environment: Your own IDE in your chosen language, screen-shared over Zoom, with your favorite test framework ready; CodePair offered if you cannot set up an IDE; using a debugger is encouraged (official backend prep PDF). AI-enabled Code Design rounds (2026) run in a HackerRank IDE with AI coding assistants and an existing repo. Frontend: browser coding in your framework (set up a page that prints the current time before the call).
coding.graded_on: Official: coding skills, code quality, conceptual thinking, adaptability, navigating blockers, communication; testing matters (TDD recommended); show alternative solutions and why you chose one. 'Clean code matters, but what's most important is how you think.' AI round: how you plan with AI, articulate prompts, and validate the result (candidate report Sep 2026).

system_design: Not a standard round for interns or most new grads; P30 Karat screens include about 20 min of rapid-fire design scenarios (scaling bottlenecks, cost estimation, unreliable third-party API, large file uploads). From P40: one 60-min system design (whiteboard, Zoom whiteboard or drawing tool) on Atlassian-flavored prompts: tagging system across Jira/Confluence/Bitbucket, top-K popular or most-engaged Confluence pages (exclude already-viewed), web crawler, scorecard service, color picker. LLD is covered by the Code Design coding round (Snake, router, booking, ratings).

behavioral.framework: Atlassian's five values: Open company, no bullshit; Build with heart and balance; Don't #@!% the customer; Play, as a team; Be the change you seek. Answer in STAR format.
what_they_look_for: Stories mapped to each of the five values (official prep PDF lists prompts per value)
User-centered decisions and the trade-offs you made for the customer
Handling difficult conversations and conflict, adapting communication style
Advocating for change and what you learned from the outcome
Owning outcomes, using expertise to drive improvements, taking initiative, helping the team succeed (management interview areas)
Concrete metrics for impact, since behavioral performance feeds leveling
Values interviewer is usually from a different department than the hiring team, so keep it non-technical unless invited
sample_questions: How have you helped make a team or individual more successful if they weren't performing well?
Have you ever had to put the team's goals above personal ambitions?
When have you advocated to push for change? What was the outcome?
How have you put the customer first? What trade-off did you make?
What's your approach when having difficult conversations? How have you resolved conflict?
What are examples when you or the team missed the mark? How did you react and fix it?
Tell me about a time you advocated for the customer (Data Engineering Intern, 2025)
How do you use agents to resolve issues in a repository? (SWE Intern, Kharagpur campus, Aug 2026)
What was a trade-off you dealt with at your last internship? (SWE Intern, Vancouver, 2026)
Give me an example of a tough or critical piece of feedback you received. (Values interview, Hello Interview, mid-level to senior manager, Jul 2026)

non_leetcode_formats: AI-enabled Code Design (HackerRank IDE + AI assistant, extend an existing repo; one Sep 2026 report: plan and implement a Spring Boot web feature with AI and explain how you validated it). Code Design / LLD in your own IDE with JUnit-style tests (Snake game, middleware router, tennis court booking, rating systems). Karat screen with rapid-fire design scenarios. Browser coding for frontend roles (tic tac toe, nested bullet list). Management and values interviews. UK graduate psychometric tests.

reported_questions.title: Activity streak: longest contiguous run with constant day-to-day difference; part 2 allows replacing one value
Minimum total cost to make all array values distinct when incrementing A[i] by 1 costs C[i]
Count bitonic subsequences (strictly up then strictly down, length 3+), mod 1e9+7
reported_questions.role: SDE1 OA (HackerRank internship drive), India, 2026 grad

reported_questions.title: Binary audit log with '?' wildcards: can it be filled so no palindromic substring of length 5+ exists
AI-assisted coding: fix a bug in a small backend web app (password feature) using the AI agent
Tennis court booking in 3 parts: assign bookings to courts, add maintenance breaks, then usage tracking
reported_questions.role: Senior SDE onsite (also P50 DSA round)

reported_questions.title: Closest common organization for a list of employees (build the org tree, LCA, write tests; follow-ups add/remove users)
Lowest common ancestor of a given set of n nodes in a parent-pointer tree
Middleware router: register paths with wildcards and resolve routes (interviewer pushed a Trie)
reported_questions.role: Senior SDE (P50, leveled P40) Code Design

reported_questions.title: Snake game LLD: snake grows every n-th food (or every 5 moves), game over on self-collision (LC 353 is Premium)
Rank teams by votes
Support agent rating system: record 1 to 5 ratings, average, sort with tie-breaks; follow-up weighted votes
All O`one data structure
reported_questions.role: Senior Backend Engineer DS round, Bengaluru

reported_questions.title: Stock price fluctuation (max price tracker with duplicate, out-of-order timestamps)
Shopping list: count department visits saved by grouping items by department
Castle rooms graph: rooms with 2+ incoming edges that point to a room leading to treasure rooms
Merge-intervals variant with sweep-line follow-ups
LRU cache plus OOP questions
Lowest common ancestor of two values in a BST
Design a tagging system across Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket (system design)
reported_questions.role: Senior SDE onsite system design (Hello Interview also shows Senior, Staff and Principal reports, Nov to Dec 2025)

reported_questions.title: AI-assisted coding round follow-up: why do you need both backend and frontend validation?
SQL: Nth highest salary without ROW_NUMBER() or RANK(); plus a 'needle in a haystack' string-search LeetCode easy
Wordle feedback string, like Bulls and Cows: generateFeedback('crane', 'train') returns 'XGGXY'
Closest common department finder: model a department hierarchy and find the lowest shared ancestor for a group of employees (LLD)
Design a Project Status Agent: AI agent that ingests DevOps, Slack and meeting transcripts and answers natural-language status questions (ML system design)

focus_topics: Hash maps with custom sorting and tie-breaks (voting, ratings)
Extensible OOP / code design with unit tests (Snake, booking, router, rating systems)
Trees: LCA in n-ary and org-chart trees
Design data structures (LRU, All O`one, stock price tracker, top-K)
DP, graphs and bitmasking for India campus OAs
AI-assisted coding in an unfamiliar codebase (2026)
System design (P40+): tagging, top-K feeds, crawlers
AI-era system design: agents over Jira/Confluence-style data (Project Status Agent, 2026)
tips: Before any coding round, open a blank project in your strongest language with a test framework (JUnit, pytest) ready; you will write, run and test code on screen share, and a debugger is allowed.
Drill the multi-part repeats (tennis court booking, Snake, agent ratings, router): finish part 1 fast and keep classes open for parts 2 and 3.
For 2026 loops, practice extending an unfamiliar repo with an AI assistant and narrate how you check its output; Atlassian says it is fine to say you are new to the language.
Write 1 to 2 STAR stories per value (5 values) with numbers; the values interviewer is often from another department, so keep stories non-technical unless asked.
Ask clarifying questions in design rounds even when the answer seems obvious; a 2026 candidate was downleveled for skipping them.
Apply in your region's window (US Sep to Mar, India Jul to Dec, ANZ Feb to Jun); review is rolling.
India campus OAs are harder than the interviews (DP, graphs, bitmask around Codeforces 1600); aim to fully solve 2+ problems.
Keep other processes going until you have a signed offer: team matching stalled for several candidates around the March 2026 layoffs.
compensation_note: Levels.fyi (Software Engineer, read 2026-10-04): US P30 average total comp $167,059/yr (base $125,340, stock $32,075/yr, bonus $9,644; 10 data points, recent offers $160k to $168k); US P40 average $248,629. India P30 average about INR 4.49M/yr (about 45 LPA; base about 2.97M); India P40 about INR 6.86M. Australia P30 average about A$142k (base about A$116k). LeetCode posts quoting '75 LPA' (2027 grad) and '85 LPA' (2026 grad) CTC likely count joining bonus and multi-year stock, so compare per-year figures.
